script:
Good morning. Here's your briefing for Wednesday, September 16.

First up, AI & Tech.

Starting with new tools you can use today, OpenAI has released its Agents A P I in public beta. This gives developers access to the managed infrastructure behind models like Codex, making it easier to build and deploy complex, long-running A I agents that can handle context, tools, and code environments. For those working with voice, OpenAI also launched G P T-Live-1. This new model in the A P I costs just five cents per minute and offers full-duplex speech, meaning it can listen and speak simultaneously, handle interruptions, and keep conversations flowing naturally. Early tests show it reduces interruptions by eighty percent compared to previous turn-based systems. This is a game-changer for building truly interactive voice agents.

Meta is rolling out "Shared Agents" for its Muse app, allowing users to create customizable agents and share them. This could be a practical tool for small businesses on Meta platforms needing specialized A I for customer support or sales workflows. If you’re a developer working with Google Cloud, there’s a new plugin specifically for A I coding agents, providing installable bundles and tools to make your agents more effective within the Google Cloud ecosystem. Also new is Open Code Review, an A I-powered command-line interface tool open-sourced by Alibaba. It's been used by tens of thousands of developers internally, identifying millions of code defects by reading full files, searching codebases, and inspecting changes for deep reviews. Finally, Solo dot I O introduced "agentdesktop," aimed at enterprises to extend A I agent governance and security to agents running on employee desktops.

On the competitive front, Cognition just pushed the Pareto frontier with S W E-2. This model achieves fifty percent on the Frontier Code one point one Main One benchmark and is an impressive sixty-four percent cheaper than its predecessor. It outperforms S W E-one point seven and Grok four point six on both score and cost. Crucially, it matches G P T-five point six Sol and Fable five at a fraction of their price, and even approaches G P T-six Astra at a quarter of the cost. This means you can get nearly top-tier autonomous code generation and bug fixing at a significantly reduced price point. In other cost-saving news, Abacus dot A I's Smaug models are claiming to cut A I agent costs by a staggering one hundred times, which could dramatically lower the barrier to deploying agents at scale.

For technical deep dives, new research confirms that scaling web video pre-training significantly improves real-world robot task performance. So what? This means that investing in larger video models and more compute for pre-training directly translates to more capable and efficient robots in practical applications like industrial unpacking. Also in research, a study on "opaque serial depth" is looking at how much unverbalized reasoning A I models perform. So what? Understanding this is critical for monitoring and debugging increasingly complex A I reasoning, especially as model internals become less transparent.

Finally, a few model and benchmark releases. North Small Translate is an open-weights research model with twenty-five billion active parameters, specialized for high-quality machine translation across fifty languages. So what? This offers a powerful new open-source option for multilingual translation. And Meta released Wearable Q A, a benchmark with thousands of questions derived from real-world wearable data. So what? This provides a standardized way to evaluate A I models' ability to reason about complex health data, which is essential for developing reliable health-focused A I applications.

Next, US Headlines.

Former President Donald Trump has suggested providing five-thousand-dollar dividend checks to Americans, a proposal House Speaker Mike Johnson said would require Congressional approval to implement. While Trump believes the payouts could easily fit into the federal budget, some lawmakers are questioning the funding source.

While on a golf trip to Ireland, former President Trump sparked discussion by stating that Irish unification would be "fantastic," a comment that deviates from the long-standing United States diplomatic stance of neutrality on the issue.

Former President Trump has also publicly downplayed expert warnings about the potential risks of artificial intelligence, emphasizing his view that the United States should not slow down development and risk losing its technological edge to rivals like China.

Meanwhile, Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson has announced he will seek re-election, framing his campaign as a test of progressive political strength in a major American city.

And finally, Immigration & Visas.

First, some news impacting H-One-B visa holders. The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a new rule that would eliminate the sixty-day grace period for H-One-B visa holders after they lose their jobs. This would significantly reduce the time individuals have to find a new employer or change their visa status, potentially requiring them to leave the U.S. much sooner than under current rules. This proposal would affect H-One-B visa holders who become unemployed.

Next, for new green card holders. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, or USCIS, has stopped sending the physical 'Welcome to America' information packets. If you are a new green card holder, you will now need to access this information online instead of receiving a mailed packet. This is a processing update for green card recipients.

Finally, a broader trend impacting the H-One-B program. Reports indicate that some tech companies are quietly moving jobs to other locations, potentially outside the U.S., as the costs associated with employing H-One-B workers continue to rise. While not a new regulation itself, this trend affects H-One-B applicants by potentially reducing job opportunities and affects employers by increasing their operational considerations for talent acquisition.

That's your briefing. Have a great day.
